ai-at-work.title: Pretend you’re sitting at Elizabeth Holmes’ desk on this weirdly detailed website
ai-at-work.excerpt: With over a thousand emails, slides, texts, and documents from the United States v. Elizabeth Holmes trial, Extend engineer Bo Lau created a website that simulates what it might have been like to rifl
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Someone built an interactive website letting you explore Elizabeth Holmes' actual emails, messages, and documents from her trial records, giving you a weird firsthand look at how the Theranos founder actually communicated. This matters because it's a masterclass in how poor internal communication, opacity, and message control can signal deeper problems in an organization, which is exactly what digital workplace leaders need to spot early. Honestly, it's the most entertaining cautionary tale about workplace culture I've seen all year, and if your company communication looks anything like Holmes' desk, you've got bigger problems than your Slack integration.

ai-at-work.title: Fired OpenAI safety researchers dispute misconduct claims, warn of chilling effect
ai-at-work.excerpt: Three fired OpenAI safety researchers dispute allegations of mishandling sensitive information, warning in an open letter that their dismissals are creating a chilling effect on the company’s AI safet
ai-at-work.dwp_take: OpenAI fired three safety researchers who then publicly challenged the company's misconduct allegations, arguing their departures will discourage others from raising concerns about AI risks. This matters because it's a textbook example of how internal dissent gets crushed in tech, and that same dynamic plays out in corporate digital workplaces every single day when people get axed for speaking up about problems. The real kicker is that OpenAI supposedly cares about AI safety, yet they're demonstrating that safety culture collapses the moment someone disagrees with leadership.

ai-at-work.title: Ben Affleck is an AI nerd, and the internet is impressed
ai-at-work.excerpt: Ben Affleck is going viral for his deep knowledge of AI, from neural networks and transformers to open weights. The actor, who sold his AI filmmaking startup to Netflix earlier this year, is proving h
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Ben Affleck sold an AI filmmaking startup to Netflix and apparently knows his transformers from his neural networks, which has the internet convinced he's secretly a technologist. This matters because it shows how AI literacy is becoming a basic expectation even for people outside tech, and workplace leaders need to stop assuming they can delegate AI understanding to the IT department. Look, if Batman can explain transformer architectures at dinner parties, your organization has no excuse for keeping AI as a mysterious black box that only specialists get to understand.

ai-at-work.title: Google brings agentic AI to Gemini, starting with businesses
ai-at-work.excerpt: Google is turning Gemini into an AI agent that can plan, execute tasks, and work across business apps and systems. The agent can delegate work to subagents, use multiple AI models, and even gets its o
ai-at-work.dwp_take: Google is rolling out agentic AI capabilities to Gemini, giving it the ability to plan tasks, execute work across business systems, and delegate to specialized subagents with its own workplace identity and email address. This matters to digital workplace pros because we're about to see AI actually doing work instead of just answering questions, which fundamentally changes how we think about automation, governance, and what employees actually do all day. Giving an AI its own email address is either the future of work or the setup for the world's most annoying Slack bot, and honestly I'm still figuring out which one keeps me up at night.

tools-tech.title: Got a Microsoft 365 subscription? Your storage is about to shrink
tools-tech.excerpt: Today, shared Microsoft 365 plans include 1 TB of OneDrive cloud storage for every family member. Microsoft is about to shrink that allotment dramatically.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Microsoft is cutting OneDrive storage from 1 TB per person to just 100 GB on shared family plans, forcing users to either pay up for more space or start playing digital tetris with their files. This matters because it affects how your organization thinks about cloud storage strategy, licensing costs, and what you tell employees about personal cloud options they're recommending to colleagues. After 30 years watching tech vendors nickel and dime users, I'll say this: the math is transparent at least, but the timing feels like they waited until everyone relied on the 1 TB before quietly moving the goal posts.

tools-tech.title: Regulators are trying to protect you from being fired by AI – here’s how
tools-tech.excerpt: Regulating AI at work is happening slowly, but it’s still stuck at the state level.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Regulators are slowly moving to protect workers from AI-driven terminations, though efforts remain fragmented across individual states rather than unified federal policy. This matters because digital workplace leaders need to know which rules apply where, and whether their AI hiring and firing systems will face legal challenges depending on geography. Honestly, watching regulators play catch-up on AI employment decisions is like watching someone try to nail jello to a tree, except the jello has lawyers and can sue you in multiple jurisdictions.

tools-tech.title: Microsoft’s new Surface Laptop Ultra finally has a starting price (you should sit down)
tools-tech.excerpt: The Surface Laptop Ultra is an AI powerhouse, with Nvidia’s new RTX Spark chip and up to 128GB of unified memory – and it’s priced for power users.
tools-tech.dwp_take: Microsoft just dropped the Surface Laptop Ultra with Nvidia's RTX Spark chip and up to 128GB of RAM, positioned as their AI-focused flagship machine. For digital workplace teams, this matters because it signals the market's serious bet on local AI processing and raises the bar for what "enterprise-grade" hardware means in 2024. Here's my take: if the price makes you reach for your chair like the headline suggests, you're probably not the target buyer, and that's actually fine because most organizations don't need AI powerhouse specs to make remote work actually function.

tools-tech.title: Google wants to be the gatekeeper for enterprise AI agents
tools-tech.excerpt: Google seems to be making a strategic play to control the AI infrastructure layer, not just roll out another shiny new agent. At its Gemini at Work 2026 event this week, the tech giant unveiled what i
tools-tech.dwp_take: Google is positioning itself as the central hub for enterprise AI agents by launching a universal agent within Gemini that connects to various business tools and systems through a single interface. This matters because digital workplace teams will need to decide whether to bet their automation strategy on Google's ecosystem or maintain flexibility across multiple vendors. Honestly, the "universal agent" pitch is as old as tech itself, and companies that remember betting everything on one platform's promises usually have some scars to show for it.

digital-culture.title: This advice from Tom Hanks changed how I work
digital-culture.excerpt: I was writing a book about the perils of recklessly chasing new things when I had an idea: I should interview Tom Hanks. I had read about how Hanks was an avid typewriter collector, and the typewriter
digital-culture.dwp_take: A Fast Company writer discovered that Tom Hanks' typewriter obsession taught him something about focused, intentional work versus the distraction treadmill we call productivity. This matters because we spend all day chasing the next collaboration platform or AI tool while forgetting that constraints sometimes beat features. Here's the irony: you need a modern digital workplace to read an article about why a typewriter is better than your digital workplace.

digital-culture.title: Technology x humanity: A conversation with Dayforce’s Amy Capellanti-Wolf
digital-culture.excerpt: The HR leader shares her take on the rise of AI, hybrid work and retaining talent.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Dayforce's Amy Capellanti-Wolf sat down to discuss how AI, hybrid work, and talent retention are reshaping the HR landscape. This matters because HR leaders are finally getting real about the fact that technology without a human strategy is just expensive software sitting in a folder. Here's the thing: anyone can buy AI tools, but keeping your people from leaving while they use those tools? That's the actual job, and it's refreshing to hear an HR leader say it out loud.

digital-culture.title: She Designed Meta’s New AI Logo. Then Came the Hate
digital-culture.excerpt: Jessica Hische knew working for Meta might upset some people. But she didn’t anticipate just how angry they would get.
digital-culture.dwp_take: Jessica Hische designed Meta's new AI logo and got absolutely hammered with online hate for her work. This matters to digital workplace folks because it highlights how design decisions in high-profile tech companies instantly become cultural flashpoints that affect everyone in the organization, not just the designer. Here's the thing: if you're doing visible work at a major tech company right now, you're basically signing up to be a lightning rod, and that's a workplace reality we need to talk about more honestly instead of pretending it doesn't happen.

digital-culture.title: Trump Administration Cuts Off Access to a Major Immigration Program for Workers at Microsoft and Adobe
digital-culture.excerpt: “There has been no company in the United States, unfortunately, that has abused this system more than Microsoft,” Vice President JD Vance said on Thursday.
digital-culture.dwp_take: The Trump administration has restricted access to H-1B visa programs for Microsoft and Adobe, with JD Vance claiming Microsoft has been the worst offender in abusing the system. This matters to digital workplace folks because tech talent sourcing just got a lot messier, and companies will need to rethink hiring strategies, relocation budgets, and retention plans overnight. Look, whether you think H-1B reform is overdue or a mistake, one thing's certain: your CHRO is about to have a very bad week fielding calls from hiring managers.

industry-news.title: Elon Musk Wants Grok Bot to Route Users to Rival AI Models
industry-news.excerpt: Elon Musk plans to expand Grok Bot with routing to rival AI models, including Claude. The move raises questions about user privacy and AI competition. The post Elon Musk Wants Grok Bot to Route Users
industry-news.dwp_take: Musk is building Grok to direct users toward competing AI models like Claude instead of keeping them locked in his walled garden. This matters because it signals a shift away from the typical AI vendor lock-in strategy, which could reshape how enterprises evaluate and deploy AI tools across their digital workplace stacks. It's either visionary generosity or the smartest way to look magnanimous while collecting data on where users actually want to go anyway.

industry-news.title: Anthropic Launches Claude Haiku 5.5 With API Prices Starting at $0.10
industry-news.excerpt: Anthropic launches Claude Haiku 5.5 with lower API pricing, stronger benchmark results and new options for developers building cost-efficient AI agents. The post Anthropic Launches Claude Haiku 5.5 Wi
industry-news.dwp_take: Anthropic just dropped Claude Haiku 5.5 with API pricing that starts at ten cents, making it cheaper to build AI agents without sacrificing performance. This matters because workplace teams are finally getting access to capable AI models that won't crater your IT budget, which means more organizations can actually experiment with automation instead of just talking about it. Honestly, watching AI pricing crater faster than enterprise software licensing used to inflate is the most satisfying thing to happen in tech in years.

industry-news.title: No Coding Needed: Google’s New AI Tool Builds Games From Your Ideas
industry-news.excerpt: Google launches Playground, an AI game-building platform that turns text prompts into playable games without coding. Here's how it works and who can use it. The post No Coding Needed: Google’s New AI
industry-news.dwp_take: Google just launched Playground, an AI tool that generates playable games from text descriptions without requiring any coding skills. This matters to digital workplace folks because it democratizes game-based learning and employee engagement tools that previously required expensive developers or technical expertise. Here's the thing though: just because you can prompt an AI to build something doesn't mean it'll be good, and workplace learning teams are about to discover the difference between "it works" and "people actually want to use this."

industry-news.title: Amazon’s New Alexa Tablets Start at $229: What’s Changing for Fire Owners
industry-news.excerpt: Amazon unveils three new Alexa tablets starting at $229.99, with Google Play access, Alexa+ features, and major changes for Fire tablet owners. The post Amazon’s New Alexa Tablets Start at $229: What’
industry-news.dwp_take: Amazon just dropped a new line of Alexa tablets starting at $229.99 with Google Play access and some fresh Alexa+ features, marking a significant shift in their tablet strategy. For digital workplace folks, this matters because tablets are increasingly part of our hybrid work ecosystems, and Amazon finally making their devices less walled-off means better integration with enterprise tools your teams probably already use. After years of Fire tablets feeling like they belonged in a gated community, Amazon's basically saying "fine, we'll play nice with the other kids" and honestly, it only took them a decade.
